cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: The Pattern
cards.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Nobody received my meeting email. This office has stopped communicating.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in your drafts. You forgot to send it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. And nobody noticed. Our entire communication system depends on my memory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send it. Go and have your lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're covering communications while I'm absent. We need a succession plan before I take a sandwich.

relationship.evidence: B2 locates the mundane mistake and B4 offers to fix it while A eats, a credible helpful participant.

heightening.evidence: B4 solution becomes A5 evidence that ordinary lunch requires institutional succession planning.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 before-a-sandwich exaggeration is earned by B4 lunch offer; the added A3 command is clumsy.
